chunks: As-Sayyid al-Sharif says: I say: 'Al-ghafirah' here means abundance and multitude, from their saying regarding a large crowd: 'al-jamm al-ghafir' or 'al-jama' al-ghafir'.

And it is narrated as '‘afwatan min ahli aw mal' (a choice from the people or wealth), and 'al-'ifuwah' means the best or selected part of something; it is said: 'I ate the 'ifuwah of the food,' meaning its best part.

And how beautiful is the meaning intended by Him (peace be upon him) in His saying: 'And whoever withholds his hand from his kin...' until the end of the speech, for he who withholds his help from his kin only withholds the benefit of one hand; but when he needs their support and is compelled to seek their assistance, they stay back from helping him and lag behind in responding to his call, thus preventing the mutual support of many hands and the vigorous advance of numerous feet.

key_terms.الْعِفْوَةُ: The best or selected part of something

ai.seo_question: What is the linguistic meaning of 'al-ghafirah' and the ethical lesson of withholding help from kin?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi elucidates 'al-ghafirah' as abundance, contrasting the singular benefit of withholding one's hand with the strategic necessity of maintaining kinship ties for mutual aid. This commentary underscores the pragmatic wisdom of the Imam, illustrating that isolating oneself from family results in the loss of the 'numerous hands and feet' required for collective support and defense.
